# Shepody (04, engineer) — BAD-080

## Brief
Make `test/collabdelivery.test.js` pass on Windows. It is green on macOS (1829 tests, 0 fail) and fails 5 on `windows-latest` in CI — all five in this one new file, all structural assertions over `main.js` and `renderer/app.js` source text:

```
not ok 285 - main's collab:push decides from the snapshot, and reads only to bootstrap one
not ok 286 - main's info poller stands aside for a room it is mid-delivery to
not ok 287 - both clients hold the booth tick on the same three terms
not ok 288 - the 20s focus poll is held on collabIdleBeat's own words, in both clients
not ok 289 - the renderer marks the push in flight, and leaves the two edge beats alone
```

The failing run: https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/actions/runs/35121035209/job/104878653882 (PR #386, branch `fix/bad-080-hot-seat`, which is this worktree and is already pushed).

## The cause

The repo has **no `.gitattributes`**, so GitHub's `windows-latest` runner checks the tree out with CRLF. The file's helpers then look for bare `\n`:

- `bodyOf()` at `test/collabdelivery.test.js:45-52` finds a function's end with `src.indexOf('\n' + indent + '}\n')` — on Windows the text is `}\r\n`, so `close` is -1 and the assertion at :50 fails.
- `holdLines()` at :68-72 matches `/( *const recording = .+;\n *if \(!recording && collabTakeInFlight\(\)\) return;)/` — `.` matches the `\r` but the literal `\n` then has nothing to match, so the regex fails.

Any other `\n` literal in a regex or `indexOf` over the source strings has the same problem.

## The fix

Normalize the line endings **once, at read time**, so every assertion in the file is CRLF-proof rather than patching them one at a time. `read()` is at :30 (`const read = (...p) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(REPO, ...p), 'utf8');`) and feeds `ROOM_TS`, `SYNC_JS`, `MAIN_JS`, `APP_JS` and whatever else the file now reads. Strip `\r` there.

Add a short comment saying why — a future reader should not have to rediscover that this file asserts over source text and therefore cannot trust the checkout's line endings.

Then sweep the rest of the file for any *other* platform assumption of the same kind (a path built with `/`, an `os.EOL`, anything comparing byte offsets) and fix what you find. Do not restructure the tests, do not change what they assert, and do not touch any file outside `test/collabdelivery.test.js` — in particular **do not add a `.gitattributes`**; normalizing the whole repo's line endings is a much larger decision than this ticket, and if you think it is the right one, `proposal file` it instead.
